Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug report indicates that the method org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.moment.c0.m0(double[] values, double[] weights, double mean, int begin, int length) ignores the length parameter and uses the whole dataset instead. While this specific method isn't individually retrieved, the related method in the Variance class evaluate(double[] values, double[] weights, double mean, int begin, int length) exhibits similar behavior.

Examining Variance.evaluate(values, weights, mean, begin, length), we see that the loop from lines 513 to 517 respects the begin and length parameters, iterating from i=begin to i < begin+length. However, the problem lies in the summation of weights from lines 519-522, where the code sums weights over the entire weights array (from index 0 to weights.length), ignoring the begin and length parameters. This leads to an incorrect denominator in the variance calculation, effectively disregarding the provided segment length and segment start.

In contrast, the Mean.evaluate(values, weights, begin, length) method correctly handles the length parameter by using its own Sum.evaluate(weights, begin, length) which sums weights only in the specified segment. The Sum.evaluate(weights, begin, length) method confirms that summation respects the begin and length, iterating from i=begin to i < begin+length.

Thus, the root cause is that Variance.evaluate(values, weights, mean, begin, length) incorrectly sums all weights instead of just the weights in the segment [begin, begin+length). This causes the variance calculation to be distorted when only a subarray segment is intended, matching the bug report and test failure scenario. The workaround is to limit the weights sum to the segment, similar to how Mean class does it.

The test failure in VarianceTest.testEvaluateArraySegmentWeighted() is caused by this bug, as the method call stat.evaluate(testArray, testWeightsArray, 0, 5) sends a segment, but the weights summation ignores the segment length, leading to an incorrect value compared to stat.evaluate(arrayZero, weightZero) which uses the entire arrays without segment parameters. This confirms the bug occurs in Variance.evaluate double[] segment handling.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
